name: Light strand text
description: Tall, heavy letters filled with hundreds of fine vertical strands of light, steel blue to white, brightening and fading as light slides down them, with a few warm threads running through and a glow along the lower edges.

name: Light waves
description: A glossy sheet of fine parallel ridges folding in slow, deep waves, each ridge catching the light so the lines shimmer and bunch where the sheet turns, with an iridescent sheen sliding across the folds.

name: Glass tube
description: A thick, see-through tube of glowing glass drawing itself along any path, with bright edges, a soft core and overlaps that show through each other, coloured from one end to the other.

name: Sticker wrap
description: Any outline (SVG path data) made into a still die-cut sticker: fitted to the frame, given a thick white border, a coloured glossy face and a soft shadow, and tilted a little. Give it a logo's or an asset's silhouette.

name: Speech sticker
description: A still die-cut speech bubble sticker saying a few words, in a white border with a glossy face and a soft shadow, tilted a little.

name: Sticker label
description: A still rounded-rectangle label sticker, like one on a laptop lid: a bold title over a small line, in a white border with a glossy face and a soft shadow, tilted a little.

name: Die-cut sticker
description: A still die-cut sticker with a label: a burst, heart, star, circle, pill or bolt in a thick white border, with a glossy face and a soft shadow, tilted a little. Drops into a page or a scene as it is.

controls.l: Shape (0 burst, 1 heart, 2 star, 3 circle, 4 pill, 5 bolt)

name: Sticker cutout
description: Any picture or SVG with transparency turned into a still die-cut sticker: its own colours inside a white border grown from its outline, a soft drop shadow, a gloss band and, if wanted, a touch of holographic foil. Made for dropping artwork into a page or scene.

name: Handheld
description: While the shot holds, the camera is held by hand: it drifts, sways and rolls a little around the framing, from a documentary's gentle float to found-footage shake, with footsteps if the operator walks.

name: Dolly zoom
description: The vertigo shot: the subject holds its size in the middle of the frame while the background behind it stretches towards the camera or falls away, as when a camera dollies one way and zooms the other.

name: Crash zoom
description: While the shot holds, the camera crashes in on a point (a face, a stare, a detail) in a few sudden steps, each landing with a kick, and stays there.

controls.l: Zoom onto (0–1 across the framing, y down)

name: Ken Burns
description: While the shot holds, the camera drifts slowly across the framing, easing from one zoom to another as it pans.

name: Cut
description: The camera jumps straight to the next framing, taking no time.

name: Punch zoom
description: The camera punches into the last framing, blurring every way, and cuts to the next one settling out of a punched-in view.

name: Whip pan
description: The camera whips off the last framing toward the next in a streak of motion blur and whips in onto it, cutting at the blurriest moment.

name: Glide
description: The camera eases across from the last framing to the next, zooming and turning smoothly on the way.

name: Flare wipe
description: An anamorphic lens flare sweeps across the frame, its streak and bloom washing over the cut, and the next picture is left behind it. Loops back and forth; or turn Animate off and set Progress.

name: Opening credits
description: A film's opening credits: one card at a time, a small tracked lead over a name, each fading in while it eases larger and fading out, ending on the film's title.

controls.d: A film by: Ada Lovelace; Starring: Grace Hopper; With: Alan Turing; Music by: Delia Derbyshire; # The Long Way Home

name: Trailer title slam
description: A film-trailer title hit: brushed-metal letters slam down out of the dark with a flash, a shake and a burst of dust, a lens flare glints across them, they hold and fade back to black.

name: Cinema projector
description: A picture showing on a cinema screen in a dark auditorium: it flickers and weaves in the gate, a dusty projector beam fans down onto it, its light spills onto the curtains, and a row of heads sits silhouetted in front.
